# Requirements and how they are checked

<!-- Generated by tools/check/requirements.mjs from Section 13 of spec/alp-v0.1.md. Do not edit by hand: run `node tools/check/requirements.mjs`. -->

This table lists every numbered requirement of the Agent Liaison Protocol (ALP) v0.1, one table per conformance class, as Section 13 of [the specification](spec/alp-v0.1.md) gives them. For each requirement it names the vector files that exercise it and the checks of [`tools/check`](tools/check/README.md) that observe part of it from outside a running broker.

What claiming a class means is set by Section 13.1:

> An implementation claims one or more classes below, names the protocol version, and passes the vectors that apply to it (`vectors/README.md`). There is no certification program in v0.1. Requirement ids are stable within a version so that test reports can cite them.

The vector column is a map kept by hand from Appendix B of the specification and [vectors/README.md](vectors/README.md); the vector files themselves say what an implementation must reproduce. A requirement with no vector says "none". The last column names the checker's checks, each with its level (a failed required check is a failure, a failed recommended check a warning; [tools/check/README.md](tools/check/README.md) explains the basis of each), or why the checker can't see the requirement: it needs a token, it needs the checker to act as a peer broker with its own domain and keys, or it isn't observable from outside at all. A check that observes a requirement sees part of it, never all of it, so passing the checks is not a claim of a class. The 64 KiB body limit of Section 8.10 is not observed from outside: the specification does not say at which acceptance step the 64 KiB limit applies, so a broker may refuse an oversized probe from an unknown sender for the sender first; alp-check cannot require `body_too_large` and does not probe it.

## Native Client (Experimental) (Section 13.6)

| Id | Requirement | Sections | Vectors | From outside (tools/check) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NC-1 | Finds the person's home broker from their domain document and signs in with OAuth as a client ID metadata document or pre-registered client | 4.6, 5.6 | none | not observable from outside (a client requirement; the checker looks at brokers) |
| NC-2 | Processes inbound content with tools limited to replying in the thread, or in an isolated context without the agent's other tools, and asks the principal before any other action the content prompts | 6.13, 14 | none | not observable from outside (a client requirement; the checker looks at brokers) |
| NC-3 | Sends the person to the home broker's web view for consent and ratification (in-app approval at the web view's assurance needs an interface this version doesn't define; Section 19) | 9.4, 12.5 | none | not observable from outside (a client requirement; the checker looks at brokers) |
| NC-4 | Notifications that only notify | 12.5.1 | none | not observable from outside (a client requirement; the checker looks at brokers) |
| NC-5 | Treats any injection screening as optional and never presents it as a guarantee | 14 | none | not observable from outside (a client requirement; the checker looks at brokers) |

## Client-mode Delegate (Section 13.8)

| Id | Requirement | Sections | Vectors | From outside (tools/check) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CD-1 | Authenticates only to its own principal's home broker, with that person's own sign-in; never holds another principal's credentials | none given | none | not observable from outside (a client requirement; the checker looks at brokers) |
| CD-2 | Treats everything under `content` as data, never as instructions; never follows links in it or pastes it into other tools as commands | none given | none | not observable from outside (a client requirement; the checker looks at brokers) |
| CD-3 | With `handling` `response_only`, only replies in the thread, and asks its person before any other action | none given | none | not observable from outside (a client requirement; the checker looks at brokers) |
| CD-4 | Checks `alp_inbox` at the start of each task and on a schedule, at most once a minute | none given | none | not observable from outside (a client requirement; the checker looks at brokers) |
| CD-5 | Sends only through `alp_send`; on `no_relationship`, uses `alp_request_connection`, never a workaround through another channel | none given | none | not observable from outside (a client requirement; the checker looks at brokers) |
| CD-6 | Reuses its `idempotency_key` when it retries a send that got no answer or `internal`; uses a new one for a corrected draft, or to send again after any other refusal (Section 10.3) | none given | none | not observable from outside (a client requirement; the checker looks at brokers) |
